source_text: Ὅτι οὐ δεῖ μετὰ δυὸ ἑβδομάδας τῆς Τεσσαρακοστῆς δέχεσθαι εἰς τὸ φώτισμα.
thought_title: No baptismal enrollment after the second week of Lent
orientation: The Council of Laodicea is issuing its own decrees, and this canon sets a deadline for admitting candidates to baptism during Lent.
pass_a_gloss: That it is not necessary after two weeks of Lent to receive into the baptism.

choices.why: The noun φώτισμα means baptism as the act of enlightening; the glossary maps φωτιζόμενοι to 'those being baptized', so the related noun is rendered 'baptism' to keep the same English family.
The glossary requires 'Lent' for Τεσσαρακοστή, the forty-day fast before Pascha.
The infinitive is passive in form but active in sense here, meaning to admit or accept someone as a candidate; 'receive' preserves the verb's basic sense.
The numeral and noun are straightforward; 'two weeks' is the natural English equivalent.

pass_b_english: No one is to be received into the baptism after two weeks of Lent.

last_rejected.why: μετα + accusative means 'after' in time, but context demands 'within/after the first two weeks'—the canon limits when baptism may begin, not when it ends. 'After two weeks' misreads as permission after that point.
last_rejected.fix: No one is to be received for baptism once two weeks of Lent have passed.
last_rejected.ruling: μετὰ + acc. means 'after'; 'after two weeks of Lent' is literal. The claim disputes canon interpretation, not translation accuracy.
